question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x?$ Assume that $n$ represents any integer.

I. The function has asymptotes at $x=\pi n.$

II. $\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})=\operatorname{tan}⁡(x+\frac{3\pi }{4}).$

III. The function is strictly increasing on the interval $(-\frac{3\pi }{2},-\frac{\pi }{2}).$
question.worked_solution:
Let's recall the graph of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14260557/assets/31b430f003171dcc04a8f17402d6035fbbc305c244d3676bbf5da83fa447bd50.png)

Let's examine each statement.

- Statement I is false. The function $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ has asymptotes at $x=\frac{\pi }{2}+\pi n.$

- Statement II is true. The function $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ has period $\pi .$ So, $\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})=\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4}+\pi )=\operatorname{tan}⁡(x+\frac{3\pi }{4}).$

- Statement III is true. The function is strictly increasing on each interval                    $(-\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ).$ If we take $n=-1$ we get the interval $(-\frac{3\pi }{2},-\frac{\pi }{2}).$
